findings.evidence: grep hits: lines 7-9 are all `public import`; the new theorem statements at lines 61, 99, 107, and 114 mention only `IsCompletelyMonotone`, while `Closure` is used only in the proof at line 116 via `.pow`.
findings.fix: Publicly import only the declarations needed in theorem statements, e.g. `TauCeti.Analysis.CompletelyMonotone.Basic`, and make `Closure`, `WithinZpow`, and `ContDiff.Operations` plain private imports for the proofs.
findings.issue: The module publicly re-exports proof-only dependencies (`Closure`, `WithinZpow`, and `ContDiff.Operations`), so importing the reciprocal theorem also exposes unrelated closure and calculus APIs.

findings.evidence: grep hits: roadmap Part B acceptance/building-block area is lines 173-195; PR file docs at lines 16-17 and 41-42 describe `(a + t)^{-k}`, but the only exposed power theorem is line 115: `IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => ((a + t) ^ k)⁻¹)`.
findings.fix: Add the zpow characteristic theorem, e.g. `IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => (a + t) ^ (-(k : ℤ)))`, proved by rewriting with `zpow_neg`/`zpow_natCast`, and keep the inverse-of-nat-power form as a restatement if desired.
findings.issue: The public power theorem exposes only `fun t => ((a + t) ^ k)⁻¹`, but the PR/roadmap-facing API advertises integer powers `t ↦ (a + t)^{-k}`; downstream users with zpow goals cannot use the named building block without an extra bridge theorem.

summary: The new reciprocal facts are useful, but the exposed module surface is too broad and the advertised integer-power form is not actually part of the public API.
